rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (base_speed 1.3, kp 3.5, kd 0.6) scored 556.7, the best so far. Its oval finished 20/20 at 2.03 s, s-bend finished 9/20 with progress 0.88, and slalom ended off track in 20/20 at progress 0.30 with max_error 0.064 and 1.15 line-loss events. Iteration 2 (base_speed 1.2, otherwise identical) scored 521.7, lower. The oval fell to 19/20, and the s-bend finish rate dropped from 45% to 25% with progress 0.86. Only the slalom improved, from 0.30 to 0.39 progress. Net, lowering speed cost more on the s-bend and oval than it gained on the slalom, so I am returning to base_speed 1.3. The Evaluator's conditional plan (keep 1.2 and test kp 3.8) does not hold cleanly, because the s-bend progress fell rather than rose. I am therefore reverting speed and testing steering authority at the best speed. Change: kp 3.5 to 3.8 and kd 0.6 to 0.7, with base_speed 1.3, ki 0, line_loss last_direction, and geometry unchanged. The higher kp gives a harder correction at the tight arcs where the robot currently leaves the tape at about 0.06 m. The slightly higher kd is there to damp the extra gain and limit the oscillation that rose on the s-bend (0.37). Expected result: s-bend finish rate above 45%, slalom progress above 0.30, and a score above 556.7. The oval should still finish near 2.0 s. Risks: kp 3.8 may increase steering oscillation and push the oval off track. Hypotheses: (a) steering authority, not speed, limits the slalom, so progress rises with kp; (b) line_loss_events fall below 1.0 on bends. Measurements requested: all metrics, so I can compare per-track max_error, line-loss events and completion_time against iterations 1 and 2. If the oval shows off-track exits or steering_oscillation rises well above 0.37, next step is kp 3.5 with kd 0.8 rather than further kp increases. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06 and line_loss_events near 1.0, test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' only if the last valid signal shows a consistent one-sided exit.
